overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation: a committee member's filing of two OML complaints with the chair, which the chair forwarded to the full committee, was not improper deliberation.

allegations.summary: A committee member allegedly deliberated outside a posted meeting by filing two Open Meeting Law complaints with the chair, knowing they would go to the full committee.
allegations.key_passage: For the reasons stated above, we find that Mr. Lavoie did not improperly deliberate when he filed two Open Meeting Law complaints with the Committee.

allegations.summary: The complaints allegedly included opinions on other members' conduct and policy-violation claims beyond the Open Meeting Law, which was said to be an improper communication.
allegations.key_passage: we find the content of the complaints was reasonably limited to allegations that Mr. Lavoie believed constituted violations of the Open Meeting Law or information he believed was relevant to his Open Meeting Law complaints.
